[Machine Learning on AWS with SageMaker and Bedrock](https://carpentries-incubator.github.io/ML_with_AWS_SageMaker/) teaches researchers how to run ML and AI work on AWS: where to store the data, which compute to use, how to launch and monitor a job, and how to estimate and manage the cost. SageMaker trains, fine-tunes and runs your own models, launched from a small notebook instance that acts as the controller while the demanding work runs on separate instances started for each job. Bedrock calls models AWS hosts through an API.

The 15 episodes run in four parts: orientation and setup (pricing, an S3 bucket, the controller notebook); SageMaker training, hyperparameter tuning, and a LoRA fine-tune of a vision-language model; RAG with Bedrock and with SageMaker Processing jobs; and cleanup and cost tracking. No previous AWS experience is needed.

::: {.callout-tip}
## UW-Madison Cloud Users
A personal AWS account is fine for this workshop. However, for **long-term research use**, we recommend switching to a **UW-provisioned AWS account**. You'll get institutional pricing via [Internet2 NET+](https://internet2.edu/cloud/cloud-solutions-community/net-plus/), [lower overhead on grants](https://rsp.wisc.edu/proposalprep/cloudComputeInfo.cfm) (26% instead of 55.5% — saving ~$2,950 per $10k in cloud costs), data protection agreements (including BAA for HIPAA), and dedicated support from the [Public Cloud Team](https://kb.wisc.edu/page.php?id=109785). NIH-funded researchers can get additional discounts through the [STRIDES Initiative](https://kb.wisc.edu/109813).

**[Request a UW AWS account](https://kb.wisc.edu/sbsedirbs/page.php?id=104090)** | **[Why use a UW account?](https://kb.wisc.edu/page.php?id=109785)** | **[Full details: UW Cloud Services](https://uw-madison-datascience.github.io/ML-X-Nexus/Toolbox/Compute/UW-Cloud-Services.html)**
:::

#### Cost estimate
Run as written, the exercises cost each learner **a few dollars, about $10 on an account of your own**, with the CPU and GPU training jobs, hyperparameter tuning, the LoRA fine-tune and RAG inference included. Every job is estimated before launch, capped in runtime, and read back from the bill afterwards, and the [final episode](https://carpentries-incubator.github.io/ML_with_AWS_SageMaker/15_Resource-management-cleanup.html) covers cleanup and cost tracking. UW-Madison sessions (ML Marathon, Research Bazaar) use a shared account with guard rails that block the expensive mistakes. On an account of your own, new accounts start on a free plan that does not cover GPUs, so you need the paid plan and a GPU quota request filed three to four weeks ahead; the lesson's [setup page](https://carpentries-incubator.github.io/ML_with_AWS_SageMaker/index.html#setup-complete-before-the-workshop) has the steps.

#### Prerequisites
The lesson assumes you are comfortable with Python and Jupyter and know the basics of model training, hyperparameter tuning, fine-tuning, embeddings and RAG. It uses those methods but does not teach them.

- [**Workshop**: Basic Python Programming](https://uw-madison-datascience.github.io/ML-X-Nexus/Learn/Workshops/Intro-Python_Gapminder.html)
- [**Workshop**: Intro to Machine Learning](https://uw-madison-datascience.github.io/ML-X-Nexus/Learn/Workshops/Intro-ML_Sklearn.html)
- [**Notebook**: Exploring Fact-Based QA with RAG: Romeo and Juliet](https://uw-madison-datascience.github.io/ML-X-Nexus/Learn/Notebooks/2025-05-07_RAG-Romeo-Juliet.html), for the RAG episodes

#### Estimated time to complete
**About 10 hours** of teaching and exercises for the core episodes, 12 with the three optional ones (pushing notebooks to GitHub, RAG on a notebook GPU, and the same jobs from the terminal). The fine-tuning episode alone is three hours.

## Related resources
- [**Notebook**: Fine-tuning with LoRA: Colab, CHTC, or AWS](https://uw-madison-datascience.github.io/ML-X-Nexus/Learn/Notebooks/Finetuning-with-LoRA.html) – The lesson's fine-tuning episode on Google Colab's free T4, no AWS account needed, with a side-by-side of running the same fine-tune on AWS SageMaker and CHTC.
- [**Compute**: UW-Madison Cloud Services (AWS, GCP, Azure)](https://uw-madison-datascience.github.io/ML-X-Nexus/Toolbox/Compute/UW-Cloud-Services.html) – Institutional discounts, lower grant overhead, data protections, research credits, and how to request a UW cloud account.
- [Public Cloud Team office hours](https://kb.wisc.edu/101516): Drop-in hours on Thursdays, 2–3:15 PM via Zoom. Get answers to cloud-related questions from the RCI and Public Cloud Team.
- [Introduction to AWS for Researchers (RCI)](https://researchci.it.wisc.edu/introduction-to-aws-for-researchers/): UW-Madison RCI’s guide to getting started with AWS for research.
- [**Compute**: Intro to GCP for ML/AI](https://uw-madison-datascience.github.io/ML-X-Nexus/Learn/Workshops/Intro-GCP.html) – Parallel workshop covering similar cloud ML concepts using GCP infrastructure.
- [**Compute**: BadgerCompute](https://uw-madison-datascience.github.io/ML-X-Nexus/Toolbox/Compute/BadgerCompute.html) – UW–Madison’s lightweight, NetID-authenticated Jupyter service for short interactive sessions and classroom use. Includes a 4-hour runtime limit (which may sometimes beat the free version of Colab).
- [**Compute**: Google Colab](https://uw-madison-datascience.github.io/ML-X-Nexus/Toolbox/Compute/GoogleColab.html) - Learn how to use Google Colab for machine learning workflows.
- [**Compute**: Center for High Throughput Computing (CHTC)](https://uw-madison-datascience.github.io/ML-X-Nexus/Toolbox/Compute/CHTC.html) - Learn how to use CHTC for machine learning jobs.
- [**Talk**: Deploying RAG in Bedrock vs. Local: WattBot 2025 Case Study](https://uw-madison-datascience.github.io/ML-X-Nexus/Applications/Videos/Forums/mlx_2026-02-17.html): Case study of a RAG system deployed on Bedrock and compared with a local open-model deployment.
- [**Project**: WattBot 2025](https://uw-madison-datascience.github.io/ML-X-Nexus/Projects/ML-Marathon/WattBot-2025.html): The ML Marathon challenge used as the workshop's RAG example.
